set.st: In January 1902 two hunters found a bronze sun-dial and compass at an old Indian village site on the southeast shore of Green Bay just above Point Sable. The 1902 wire story said Reuben Gold Thwaites thought it had belonged to the Jesuit missionary Allouez. The State Historical Society's own published caption (1902) does not name Allouez: it calls the piece 'apparently of the 17th century' and says it 'may have been lost by some fur-trader or missionary.'

src: Collections of the State Historical Society of Wisconsin, vol. 16 (1902), plate facing p. 64: 'Combined Bronze Sun-Dial and Compass'

set.pl: Marble Grove, on the ridge between Spirit Lake and Marble Lake (Smith 1902)
pinev: Marble Grove, ridge between Spirit Lake and Marble Lake (Smith 1902; Sharp 1885). Placed on land on the wooded ridge (1930 ortho, 2020 Iowa lidar hillshade); the suggested 43.473,-95.130 falls in Marble Lake itself.

tw-ia-spirit-lake-marble-gold-1857.t: Neither Sharp (1885) nor Smith (1902) mentions gold or money; the $1,500 rests on Laird (1927) alone.
src: R. A. Smith, A History of Dickinson County, Iowa (1902), Marble settlement
